title: Melde et problem og be om tiltak — report a problem and request action
goal: Select observable facts, describe their effect, request one proportionate remedy, and confirm the next step.

objectives.statement: Select observable facts, describe their effect, request one proportionate remedy, and confirm the next step.

spans.value: Nora has recently moved into a rented flat. On Monday morning, she notices water inside the cupboard under the kitchen sink. She calls Erik, the building caretaker.
Hei, Erik. Det drypper fra røret under kjøkkenvasken.

blocks.translation: Hi, Erik. Water is dripping from the pipe under the kitchen sink.

spans.value: Har det kommet mye vann?
Ikke så mye, men bunnen i skapet blir våt, og jeg kan ikke oppbevare noe der.

blocks.translation: Not very much, but the bottom of the cupboard is getting wet, and I can’t store anything there.

spans.value: Jeg forstår. Kan du sette en bøtte under røret?

blocks.translation: I understand. Can you put a bucket under the pipe?

spans.value: Ja, det kan jeg. Kan du komme og se på det i dag?

blocks.translation: Yes, I can. Can you come and look at it today?

spans.value: Ja. Jeg kommer mellom klokka fire og fem.

blocks.translation: Yes. I’ll come between four and five.

spans.value: Fint. Så du kommer hit mellom klokka fire og fem, og jeg setter en bøtte under røret fram til da?

blocks.translation: Good. So you’ll come here between four and five, and I’ll put a bucket under the pipe until then?

spans.value: Det stemmer. Ring meg igjen hvis det begynner å renne mer.

blocks.translation: That’s right. Call me again if more water starts to flow.

spans.value: Nora handles the conversation calmly and efficiently. She says what she can observe, explains the practical effect, asks for one reasonable action, and checks what will happen next. These four parts form a useful pattern:
observable fact → effect → requested remedy → confirmed next step
You can use this pattern when speaking to a landlord, caretaker, hotel employee, shop worker, delivery company, or service provider.

sections.title: Start with what you can observe

spans.value: When reporting a problem, begin with something specific that another person can understand or check. An observable fact describes a condition that you directly notice or that another person can check.
Nora says:

no.value: Det drypper fra røret under kjøkkenvasken.

en.value: Water is dripping from the pipe under the kitchen sink.

spans.value: She does not begin by guessing who caused the leak or why it happened. This keeps the conversation focused on the problem.
Compare these descriptions:

no.value: Det ligger vann på gulvet.

en.value: There is water on the floor.

no.value: Jeg ser en sprekk i vinduet.

en.value: I can see a crack in the window.

no.value: Pakken er åpen på den ene siden.

en.value: The parcel is open on one side.

no.value: Lyset på badet virker ikke.

en.value: The bathroom light does not work.

no.value: Bussen kom ikke til holdeplassen.

en.value: The bus did not come to the stop.

spans.value: Each sentence gives information that can be observed or checked.
A judgment or accusation is less useful:

no.value: Dette er elendig arbeid.

en.value: This is terrible work.

spans.value: A factual description is clearer:

no.value: Døra går ikke helt igjen.

en.value: The door does not close completely.

spans.value: Similarly:

no.value: Dere har ødelagt pakken min.

en.value: You have damaged my parcel.

spans.value: may sound accusatory if you do not know what happened. A more precise opening is:

no.value: Pakken var skadet da jeg fikk den.

en.value: The parcel was damaged when I received it.

spans.value: You do not need to hide a serious problem or sound uncertain about a fact. The aim is simply to separate what you know from what you assume.
Checkpoint: Find the factual core

Read Nora and Erik’s first exchange again. Identify the sentence that states the observable problem and the question Erik asks to establish its extent. Then write one short factual sentence for this situation: you arrive at a hotel room and see that the window cannot be closed.

This activity belongs here because a clear factual opening gives the other person enough information to respond. A successful response would describe the window itself without blaming hotel staff or guessing at the cause.
A problem report becomes more useful when you explain what the problem changes for you. The effect answers a practical question: Why does this need attention?
Nora gives two effects:

no.value: Bunnen i skapet blir våt.

en.value: The bottom of the cupboard is getting wet.

no.value: Jeg kan ikke oppbevare noe der.

en.value: I can’t store anything there.

spans.value: Common ways to describe an effect include:

no.value: Jeg kan ikke bruke …

en.value: I can’t use …

no.value: Det betyr at …

en.value: That means that …

no.value: Derfor må jeg …

en.value: Therefore I have to …

no.value: Nå blir …

en.value: Now … is becoming …

spans.value: Here are some complete problem reports with a fact and an effect:

no.value: Varmeovnen virker ikke, så rommet er veldig kaldt.

en.value: The heater does not work, so the room is very cold.

no.value: Jeg fikk feil nøkkel, og derfor kommer jeg ikke inn i boden.

en.value: I received the wrong key, and therefore I can’t get into the storage room.

no.value: Det mangler én vare i leveringen, så jeg kan ikke fullføre bestillingen.

en.value: One item is missing from the delivery, so I can’t complete the order.

no.value: Vaskemaskinen stopper etter noen minutter. Det betyr at jeg ikke får vasket klærne.

en.value: The washing machine stops after a few minutes. That means I can’t wash the clothes.

no.value: Internettforbindelsen forsvinner flere ganger om dagen, så jeg kan ikke delta i nettmøtene mine.

en.value: The internet connection drops several times a day, so I can’t participate in my online meetings.

spans.value: Keep the effect concrete. You usually do not need a long account of your frustration.
Compare:

no.value: Dette er utrolig irriterende, og hele dagen min er ødelagt.

en.value: This is incredibly annoying, and my whole day is ruined.

spans.value: with:

no.value: Jeg kan ikke låse døra, så jeg kan ikke forlate leiligheten.

en.value: I can’t lock the door, so I can’t leave the flat.

spans.value: The second sentence tells the listener exactly why action is needed.
Checkpoint: Connect the problem to its effect

Write two short sentences about a delivery. The box has arrived, but one bottle inside is broken and liquid has damaged the other items. First state only what you can observe. Then describe one practical effect.

This activity follows factual description because the listener now needs to understand the consequence. A successful response would keep the fact and effect distinct while showing a clear connection between them.
After stating the problem and its effect, say what action would help. A proportionate remedy matches the size and urgency of the problem.
Nora asks:

no.value: Kan du komme og se på det i dag?

en.value: Can you come and look at it today?

spans.value: She does not immediately demand a complete replacement of the kitchen. She asks Erik to inspect a leak that is getting the cupboard wet.
Useful request patterns are:

no.value: Kan du se på det?

en.value: Can you look at it?

no.value: Kan dere sende en ny?

en.value: Can you send a new one?

no.value: Kan dere rette feilen?

en.value: Can you correct the error?

no.value: Kan jeg få et annet rom?

en.value: Can I have another room?

no.value: Kan noen komme i dag?

en.value: Can someone come today?

spans.value: Use
du
when speaking to one person directly, including an individual employee. Use
dere
when speaking to several people or addressing an organization collectively.

no.value: Kan du sjekke låsen?

en.value: Can you check the lock?

no.value: Kan dere sjekke bestillingen min?

en.value: Can you check my order?

spans.value: A request is more effective when it names one clear action:

no.value: Kan dere gjøre noe med dette?

en.value: Can you do something about this?

spans.value: is understandable, but vague.

no.value: Kan dere sende den manglende varen?

en.value: Can you send the missing item?

spans.value: gives the business a specific remedy to consider.
The requested action should also fit the problem:

no.value: Kaffen er kald. Kan jeg få en ny kopp?

en.value: The coffee is cold. Can I have a new cup?

no.value: Nøkkelkortet virker ikke. Kan dere aktivere det på nytt?

en.value: The key card does not work. Can you activate it again?

no.value: Det er en sprekk i frontruta på leiebilen. Kan noen undersøke bilen før jeg kjører videre?

en.value: There is a crack in the windscreen of the rental car. Can someone inspect the car before I drive on?

spans.value: Notice that a proportionate request does not have to be weak. If a problem creates an immediate risk, the requested action can be urgent:

no.value: Det lukter brent fra sikringsskapet. Kan dere sende noen med en gang?

en.value: There is a burnt smell coming from the fuse box. Can you send someone immediately?

spans.value: The urgency comes from the observable fact, not from dramatic language.
Checkpoint: Add a suitable request
Return to the hotel window. You have already described that it cannot be closed. The room is becoming cold. Add one request for a practical remedy that hotel staff could reasonably provide.

This activity belongs after fact and effect because the request should respond directly to both. A successful response would ask for one clear action, such as inspecting the window or providing another room, without adding unrelated demands.
Do not end the exchange as soon as the other person says yes. Check what has been agreed: who will act, what they will do, and when it will happen.
Erik says:

no.value: Jeg kommer mellom klokka fire og fem.

en.value: I’ll come between four and five.

spans.value: Nora confirms:

no.value: Så du kommer hit mellom klokka fire og fem, og jeg setter en bøtte under røret fram til da?

en.value: So you’ll come here between four and five, and I’ll put a bucket under the pipe until then?

spans.value: Useful confirmation phrases include:

no.value: Så du kommer i ettermiddag?

en.value: So you’re coming this afternoon?

no.value: Så dere sender en ny vare i morgen?

en.value: So you’re sending a new item tomorrow?

no.value: Da venter jeg på en e-post fra dere.

en.value: Then I’ll wait for an email from you.

no.value: Skal jeg gjøre noe i mellomtiden?

en.value: Should I do anything in the meantime?

no.value: Når kan jeg forvente svar?

en.value: When can I expect an answer?

no.value: Har jeg forstått det riktig?

en.value: Have I understood correctly?

spans.value: Confirmation is not unnecessary repetition. It prevents misunderstandings.
Consider this exchange:
Vi sender noen senere.
Når kommer de omtrent?

blocks.translation: Customer: Approximately when will they come?

spans.value: The customer asks for information needed to understand the next step.
A clear confirmation might be:

no.value: Så en tekniker kommer mellom klokka seks og åtte, og jeg må være hjemme?

en.value: So a technician will come between six and eight, and I need to be at home?

spans.value: This checks both the service provider’s action and the customer’s responsibility.
Checkpoint: Confirm an agreement

Imagine that a delivery company has agreed to collect a damaged parcel tomorrow morning. Write one confirmation sentence that checks the action and time. Then add a short question asking whether you need to print a return label.
This activity comes here because agreement alone may leave practical details unclear. A successful response would restate the promised collection and identify what the customer must do next.
A strong report can be brief. It needs one useful detail at each stage.
Observable fact:

no.value: Skjermen på den nye telefonen har en mørk flekk.

en.value: The screen on the new phone has a dark spot.

spans.value: Effect:

no.value: Jeg kan ikke lese teksten i det området.

en.value: I can’t read the text in that area.

spans.value: Requested remedy:

no.value: Kan dere undersøke telefonen og bytte den hvis den er defekt?

en.value: Can you inspect the phone and replace it if it is defective?

spans.value: Lever den i butikken i dag, så undersøker vi den og gir deg svar innen fredag.

blocks.translation: Shop employee: Bring it to the shop today, and we’ll inspect it and give you an answer by Friday.

spans.value: Confirmed next step:

no.value: Så jeg leverer den i butikken i dag, og dere gir meg svar innen fredag?

en.value: So I’ll bring it to the shop today, and you’ll give me an answer by Friday?

spans.value: The same structure works in a less formal everyday situation:

no.value: Sykkellåsen sitter fast, så jeg får ikke brukt sykkelen. Kan du hjelpe meg med å åpne den?

en.value: The bicycle lock is stuck, so I can’t use the bicycle. Can you help me open it?

spans.value: Ja, jeg møter deg ved sykkelstativet etter lunsj.

blocks.translation: Friend: Yes, I’ll meet you by the bicycle rack after lunch.

no.value: Så møter du meg ved sykkelstativet etter lunsj?

en.value: So you’ll meet me by the bicycle rack after lunch?

spans.value: Giving only an emotional reaction

no.value: Det er helt håpløst!

en.value: Incorrect for this task: It’s completely hopeless!

spans.value: This communicates frustration but not the problem.
Add an observable fact:

no.value: Billettautomaten tar ikke imot kortet mitt.

en.value: The ticket machine does not accept my card.

spans.value: Reporting the fact but not the effect

no.value: Heisen virker ikke.

en.value: The lift does not work.

spans.value: This may be enough in a very simple situation, but the effect can show why help is needed:

no.value: Heisen virker ikke, og jeg får ikke båret barnevogna opp trappa alene.

en.value: The lift does not work, and I can’t carry the pram up the stairs alone.

spans.value: Describing the problem without requesting action

no.value: Jeg bestilte størrelse 40, men fikk størrelse 38.

en.value: I ordered size 40, but received size 38.

spans.value: Add the remedy:

no.value: Kan dere sende riktig størrelse?

en.value: Can you send the correct size?

spans.value: Making several unrelated demands

A focused request is easier to act on. If a meal contains the wrong side dish, ask for the correct side dish rather than combining the problem with complaints about the music, waiting time, and room temperature.

no.value: Jeg bestilte ris, men fikk poteter. Kan jeg få ris i stedet?

en.value: I ordered rice, but received potatoes. Can I have rice instead?

spans.value: Failing to confirm vague promises

no.value: Vi ordner det snart.

en.value: Incorrect for this task: We’ll sort it out soon.

spans.value: Ask what
snart
means in this situation:

no.value: Når kan jeg forvente at det er ferdig?

en.value: When can I expect it to be finished?

sections.title: Controlled practice: Build a complete report

spans.value: Write a four-part message to a landlord about a bedroom radiator that remains cold when it is switched on. State one observable fact, explain one practical effect, and request one appropriate action. The landlord replies:
En tekniker kommer i morgen mellom klokka ti og tolv.

blocks.translation: A technician will come tomorrow between ten and twelve.

spans.value: Then confirm the agreed action and time.

This activity combines the complete pattern in a familiar housing context. It is still controlled because the situation and communicative jobs are given. A successful response would contain all four parts and keep every sentence relevant to resolving the radiator problem.
Erik arrives at half past four and examines the pipe.
Pakningen er ødelagt. Jeg har ikke riktig del med meg, men jeg kan bytte den i morgen tidlig.

blocks.translation: The seal is broken. I don’t have the correct part with me, but I can replace it tomorrow morning.

spans.value: Vannet drypper fortsatt, så jeg kan ikke bruke skapet i kveld. Kan du stenge vannet til denne krana fram til i morgen?

blocks.translation: The water is still dripping, so I can’t use the cupboard this evening. Can you turn off the water to this tap until tomorrow?

spans.value: Ja, det gjør jeg nå. Jeg kommer tilbake rundt klokka ni i morgen.

blocks.translation: Yes, I’ll do that now. I’ll come back at around nine tomorrow.

spans.value: Fint. Så vannet til denne krana er stengt fram til i morgen, og du kommer tilbake rundt ni for å bytte pakningen?

blocks.translation: Good. So the water supply to this tap is shut off until tomorrow, and you’ll come back at around nine to replace the seal?

spans.value: Ja, nettopp.
Nora uses the same pattern again. The situation has changed, but her communication remains focused:

items.value: The observable fact is that the water is still dripping.
The effect is that she cannot use the cupboard that evening.
The proportionate remedy is to turn off the water to that tap temporarily.
The confirmed next step is that Erik will return at around nine and replace the seal.

spans.value: She does not introduce a new complaint. She responds to the current facts and checks the practical agreement.

Without looking back at the four-part pattern, write a short exchange about a washing machine that stops during every wash. Include an observable fact, its practical effect, and one proportionate request. After your request, use this supplied service-provider response:
Vi sender en tekniker på tirsdag mellom klokka to og fire.

blocks.translation: We’ll send a technician on Tuesday between two and four.

spans.value: Then confirm the agreed action and time. Label which of your sentences performs each of the four jobs.

prompt.value: Nora says «Det drypper fra røret under kjøkkenvasken.» Erik asks «Har det kommet mye vann?» Quote the sentence stating the observable problem and Erik’s question about its extent. Then write one short factual Norwegian sentence saying that a hotel-room window cannot be closed. Describe only the window, without blame or a guessed cause.

payload.judge_prompt: Check all three requested parts. The first two must accurately identify the problem statement and extent question from the source exchange. The hotel sentence must naturally describe the window itself as impossible to close, without blame or speculation. Accept natural Bokmål variants.

criteria.instruction: Identifies the sentence from the exchange that states the observable problem.
Identifies Erik’s question establishing the extent of the problem.
Describes the hotel-room window itself as impossible to close, without blame or a guessed cause.

prompt.value: A delivered box contains one broken bottle, and liquid has damaged the other items. Write two short Norwegian sentences. First state only an observable fact. Then state one practical effect, keeping the fact and effect distinct and clearly connected.

payload.judge_prompt: Check that the response contains two distinct, natural Bokmål sentences in the requested order. The first must report an observable condition without speculation. The second must state a practical consequence connected to that condition. Accept equivalent factual descriptions and plausible practical effects.

criteria.instruction: States only an observable fact about the broken bottle or liquid damage in the first sentence.
Describes one practical effect in the second sentence.
Keeps fact and effect distinct while making their connection clear.

prompt.value: A hotel-room window cannot be closed, and the room is becoming cold. Write one Norwegian request asking hotel staff for one clear, practical remedy that directly addresses this problem. Do not add unrelated demands.

payload.judge_prompt: Check for one natural Bokmål request naming one proportionate action that addresses the window or cold room. Accept requests to inspect or repair the window or provide another room. Reject vague, unrelated, or disproportionate demands.

criteria.instruction: Requests one clear action from hotel staff.
Requests a practical remedy that responds directly to the window problem and cold room.
Adds no unrelated demands.

prompt.value: A delivery company has agreed to collect a damaged parcel tomorrow morning. Write one Norwegian confirmation sentence that restates the promised collection and checks the time. Then ask in Norwegian whether you need to print a return label.

payload.judge_prompt: Check that the response confirms both collection of the damaged parcel and tomorrow morning, then asks whether the customer must print a return label. Accept natural Bokmål wording and either a separate label question or a clearly separated question in the same message.

criteria.instruction: Restates that the delivery company will collect the damaged parcel.
Checks that the collection will happen tomorrow morning.
Asks whether the customer needs to print a return label.

prompt.value: Write a focused Norwegian message to a landlord. State that a bedroom radiator remains cold when switched on, explain one practical effect, and request one appropriate action. The landlord replies: «En tekniker kommer i morgen mellom klokka ti og tolv.» Confirm that agreed action and time. Keep every sentence relevant to resolving the radiator problem.

payload.judge_prompt: Check for all four communicative parts: observable radiator fact, practical effect, appropriate request, and confirmation of the technician’s visit tomorrow between ten and twelve. Accept natural Bokmål variants, but require every sentence to remain relevant to resolving the radiator problem.

criteria.instruction: States that the bedroom radiator remains cold when it is switched on.
Explains one practical effect of the cold radiator.
Requests one appropriate action to resolve or inspect the radiator problem.
Confirms that a technician will come tomorrow between ten and twelve.
Keeps every sentence relevant to resolving the radiator problem.

prompt.value: Write a Norwegian report to a shop using four communicative steps. State that the order confirmation lists three lamps but only two arrived. Explain that one room still has no light. Ask the shop to send the missing lamp. The shop replies: «Vi sender den manglende lampen i morgen.» Confirm what the shop will send and when. Use delivery-related language, not housing-specific language.

payload.judge_prompt: Check for the four requested steps in natural Bokmål: the two-of-three delivery fact, the room without light, a request to send the missing lamp, and confirmation that the missing lamp will be sent tomorrow. Reject housing-specific wording that changes the shop-delivery situation.

criteria.instruction: States that only two of the three lamps arrived.
Explains that one room still has no light.
Asks the shop to send the missing lamp.
Confirms that the missing lamp will be sent tomorrow.
Uses all four communicative steps without housing-specific language.

prompt.value: Write a short Norwegian exchange about a washing machine that stops during every wash. Include one observable fact, one practical effect, and one proportionate request. Then use this service-provider response: «Vi sender en tekniker på tirsdag mellom klokka to og fire.» Add a sentence confirming the agreed action and time. Label your four sentences as Fact, Effect, Request, and Confirmation.

payload.judge_prompt: Check that four labeled Norwegian sentences perform the four requested jobs. Require an observable fact that the washing machine stops during every wash, a practical effect, a proportionate request, and confirmation that a technician will come on Tuesday between two and four. Accept natural Bokmål variants and equivalent clear labels for the four jobs.

criteria.instruction: Includes an observable fact that the washing machine stops during every wash.
Includes one practical effect of the washing-machine problem.
Includes one proportionate request addressing the washing-machine problem.
Confirms that a technician will come on Tuesday between two and four.
Labels which sentence is the Fact, Effect, Request, and Confirmation.
